newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court dismisses case against Enron.
newsitem.headline: Indian court dismisses case against Enron.

text.p: The Bombay High Court Monday dismissed a petition seeking to stop Enron Corp. of Houston from pursuing a power project on India's western coast.
"We are greatly happy about the judgment," Sanjay Bhatnagar, vice president of Enron's Indian subsidiary, Dabhol Power Co., told reporters after the ruling.
"We will concentrate on building the project," he said. Bhatnagar said work would begin within weeks.

Enron, a major natural gas and electric company, has won more than 20 lawsuits against its project. The latest appears to be the last opposition to the Dabhol project, clearing the way for its resumption, analysts said.
The court dismissed the petition, which had sought the scrapping of the project because of suspected irregularities.
The petition was filed by the Centre of Indian Trade Unions.
Dabhol Power Co. is 80 percent owned by Enron Development Corp and 10 percent each by U.S. firms Bechtel Corp. and General Electric Co.
The project, with a gross generating capacity of 2,450 megawatts, had faced several hurdles.
The first phase of the plant will have a gross generating capacity of 826 megawatts and should be on line 31 months after construction resumes.
Bhatnagar dismissed talk of large losses run up by Dabhol Power Company after work stopped last year.
"The media has been writing on losses," he said. "All I can say is that our investors, especially banks, are behind us."
